newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen as stable.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen as stable.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday with losses among blue chips and some hoteliers, and traders said large offers could stabilise prices or even push them a bit downward.
"A large supply today and yesterday has stabilised the market. Selling offers have outstripped demand and buyers will dictate prices next week," a trader with a large brokerage said.
That meant that prices of the most actively traded shares would stabilise or even go slightly down after a long and steady rise in the past few weeks, the source said.

The prices of hoteliers and some of the blue chips, like Kras confectioner, became attractive to shareholders who had bought them at a reduced price under the privatisation scheme and were now selling them with good profit.
Four of 14 active stocks were up, seven down, two remained flat and one traded for the first time. Volume was lower at 12,875 shares, turnover higher at 11.3 million kuna.
The biggest loser was Dalmatian hotelier Suncani Hvar, which went down 35 kuna to close at 80, reverting to the value held on Wednesday.
The biggest gainer was cable producer Elka, rising 60 kuna to 320, with 90 units traded.

Of Istrian hoteliers, which gained steadily for the past two weeks, Riviera lost 15 kuna to 290, Arenaturist lost 10 kuna to 280, Jadranturist lost 10 to 390, Istraturist gained 20 to 320, and Laguna remained flat at 1,550 -- all on relatively modest volumes of 200 to 600 shares each.
On the losing side was also Kras, which went down 30 kuna to close at 690, with 260 shares sold.
The most actively traded was blue chip Zagrebacka Banka, edging up 10 kuna to close at 1,010, selling 7,166 shares.
Another fully-listed Croatian company, drug firm Pliva, edged down 100 kuna to 12,400 with 156 shares sold.
Podravka was also actively traded, inching down 3.90 kuna to 269 on volume of 2,571 shares.
Zagreb hotel Intercontinental traded for the first time this year at 180 kuna, selling 138 units.
The central bank reference exchange rate was set at $1 = 5.4493 kuna to the dollar, up from 5.4433.
